source.title: A Distribution Testing Approach to Clustering Distributions
source.venue: Proceedings of Thirty Ninth Conference on Learning Theory

cards.observed_relation: The paper studies recovery of a hidden clustering of distributions under an explicit pairwise total-variation separation assumption and derives sample-complexity bounds that depend on separation, domain size, number of distributions, and cluster sizes.
cards.transferable_relation: A population separation condition does not by itself specify finite-sample recoverability; the observation budget and problem dimensions belong to the decision claim.
admissible_assays: Hold route-conditioned population laws fixed while varying declared sample budget, candidate count, or separation and report population equivalence separately from finite-budget decision error.
alternative_explanations: The exact sample-complexity dependence is specific to the studied distribution-clustering problem and should not be imported into unrelated inverse problems.
falsifiers: A proposed finite-budget criterion reports unchanged recoverability after material changes to sample budget or separation in a fixture authored to make those changes decision-relevant.
forbidden_inferences: Use of total variation in a distribution-testing theorem does not make total variation the universal metric of stochastic identifiability.

source.title: Is Multi-Distribution Learning as Easy as PAC Learning: Sharp Rates with Bounded Label Noise
source.venue: Proceedings of Thirty Ninth Conference on Learning Theory

cards.observed_relation: The paper derives different sample-complexity behavior for multi-distribution learning under bounded label noise and shows that the statistical cost depends on the number of distributions and on the benchmark, including comparison with each distribution's optimal Bayes error.
cards.transferable_relation: Finite-sample performance belongs to a declared decision problem and benchmark; changing the source family, noise model, or target benchmark can change sample requirements without changing the meaning of population distribution equality.
admissible_assays: Keep population route distributions fixed while changing the declared decision benchmark or sample budget and report the resulting risk separately from population equivalence classes.
alternative_explanations: The sharp rates arise from the specific multi-distribution classification setup and bounded-noise assumptions.
falsifiers: A criterion labeled finite-budget recoverability remains numerically and semantically invariant to changes in parameters that explicitly define its decision problem.
forbidden_inferences: Bayes error under one prior, loss, or benchmark is not a universal identifiability scalar.

source.title: Information-Theoretic Causal Bounds under Unmeasured Confounding
source.venue: Proceedings of the Fifth Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning

cards.observed_relation: The paper develops divergence-based sharp partial-identification bounds for causal effects under unmeasured confounding rather than presenting an unavailable point-identified quantity as uniquely recovered.
cards.transferable_relation: When the observation and assumption set supports an identified set or bound rather than a unique latent value, the bounded equivalence class is the result and must not be flattened into point identification or failure.
admissible_assays: Construct candidate families with observationally equivalent members and require the research output to preserve the identified set or equivalence class instead of forcing one winner.
alternative_explanations: The particular divergence bounds and causal interpretation are specific to the paper's confounding framework.
falsifiers: A purported partial-identification discipline still selects one latent candidate when several remain equivalent under the declared observation and assumptions.
forbidden_inferences: Causal partial-identification bounds do not establish a TD613 causal model or authorize importing causal divergences as universal route metrics.

source.title: Identifiability and Information-Based Inference for Epidemic Transmission Models Under Partial Observation

cards.observed_relation: The preprint analyzes identifiability and information loss in partially observed epidemic transmission models and studies how observation frequency, network coverage, and measurement accuracy affect estimability and inferential precision.
cards.transferable_relation: Observation design can change practical information and estimation precision without changing the latent process definition, so measurement regime must remain explicit in an identifiability or recoverability claim.
admissible_assays: Hold the latent route-conditioned process fixed while varying a predeclared observation regime and separately report equivalence classes, decision error, and information/precision diagnostics.
alternative_explanations: The reported information quantities and observation effects may be specific to epidemic network models and their likelihood structure.
falsifiers: A claimed observation-design effect disappears under a controlled model where only the admitted measurement regime changes, or the effect requires changing the latent process as well.
forbidden_inferences: Fisher information in an epidemic model does not establish TD613 information curvature or physical geometry.
